connection_sequence.description: Passive (normal): scan -> match sps/tps + fff0 + 9-byte manufacturer data -> decode. No connection ever required. Optional poll: connect -> service fff0 -> read fff2 (temp/hum) -> disconnect. Battery comes from the advertisement byte 7 only. Optional config/history: read/write fff1 (calibration, logging interval, firmware version); subscribe fff6 and drive fff8 to pull the logged history; fff9 clears history or disconnects politely.

manufacturer_data.description: Deliberately NO company_id filter: the temperature occupies the company-ID position of the manufacturer data, so the reported id changes with every reading. Identify by local name "sps"/"tps" + fff0 service UUID + 9-byte manufacturer data.

device.name: Inkbird IBS-TH1 / IBS-TH2 Thermometer-Hygrometer
device.notes:
Battery-powered BLE temperature/humidity sensors (IBS-TH1, IBS-TH2, and the IBS-P01B pool thermometer variant) that broadcast readings in BLE advertisement manufacturer data — no connection required for live values. Official apps: com.inkbird.inkbirdapp ("Inkbird") and the current com.inkbird.engbird ("Engbird", teardown basis below); the older com.inkbird.inkbird package was delisted from Google Play and every public mirror as of 2026-08.
Sources: the Bluetooth-Devices/inkbird-ble parser library (backs the Home Assistant core inkbird integration), which is itself copied from Ernst79's bleparser (the ble_monitor custom component), plus the library's test suite which pins the byte layout against captured advertisements; and static analysis of the official Engbird app (2026-03), which confirmed the advertisement/fff2 layouts and provided the fff1/fff6/fff8/fff9 connected-mode details below. Confidence: parser-library-derived, corroborated by raw advertisement captures in the test suite and by the official app; not re-verified against hardware here.
ADVERTISEMENT QUIRK — there is NO company ID. The manufacturer-specific AD structure (type 0xFF) is 9 bytes and the temperature occupies the two bytes where the Bluetooth company identifier would normally sit. Stacks therefore report the temperature as the "company id" (e.g. a reading of 20.44 °C surfaces as manufacturer_data key 2044 = 0x07FC). Two consequences: (1) discovery must NOT key on a fixed company id — every distinct reading appears as a distinct manufacturer-data entry, and consecutive readings can show up as multiple changed entries; (2) match on local name ("sps" / "tps") plus advertised service UUID 0000fff0 plus the 9-byte total length instead.
ON-AIR MANUFACTURER DATA (9 bytes, offsets from the start of the AD structure content, i.e. including the pseudo company-ID bytes):
  bytes 0-1: temperature, signed int16 LE, /100.0 °C
             (proven: capture fc 07 c7 12 00 c8 3d 56 06 ->
             0x07FC = 2044 -> 20.44 °C, inkbird-ble test_sps)
  bytes 2-3: humidity, uint16 LE, /100.0 %  (0x12C7 = 4807 -> 48.07 %)
  bytes 4-6: secondary channel — byte 4 is a channel-layout selector
             (0-3) and bytes 5-6 a signed int16 LE /100.0 value:
               selector 0: temp = bytes 0-1, humidity = bytes 2-3
               selector 1: temp = bytes 5-6, humidity = bytes 2-3,
                           external probe temp = bytes 0-1
               selector 2: temp = bytes 0-1, humidity = bytes 2-3,
                           external humidity = bytes 5-6
               selector 3: temp = bytes 5-6, external temp = bytes 0-1,
                           external humidity = bytes 2-3
             The app clamps a negative battery byte to zero and reads
             bytes 5-6 as signed.
  byte 7:    battery percent 0-100  (0x56 = 86)
  byte 8:    onboarding transport selector: 0x06 makes the app's scanner
             connect and read live data once on fff2; other values,
             including observed 0x08, stay advertisement-only. This is a
             client-routing flag, NOT a hardware-revision indicator.
IBS-TH2/P01B ("tps") uses the same 9-byte layout; humidity reads 0 on units without a humidity sensor and the parser only reports it when non-zero. Readings with humidity > 100 % are corrupt packets and should be dropped whole (inkbird-ble issue #141).
CONNECTED MODE (optional): the same reading can be polled over GATT. Service 0000fff0-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb, characteristic 0000fff2-0000-1000-8000-00805f9b34fb (read): temperature int16 LE /100 at bytes 0-1, humidity at bytes 2-3 — i.e. the advertisement layout WITHOUT the pseudo-company-id interpretation and without the battery byte (battery is advertisement-only). The app reads humidity as a signed int16 and also consumes byte 4 as a probe/channel indicator. No pairing, bonding or authentication.
Further fff0 characteristics seen in the app (not needed for read-only monitoring):
  fff1 (read/write, 16 bytes) — device config: bytes 1-2 internal
    temp calibration offset (s16 LE, x0.01 °C), bytes 3-4 external
    probe temp calibration, bytes 5-6 humidity calibration, bytes
    7-10 logging interval (u32 LE, seconds), bytes 11 and 13 ASCII
    firmware version digits ("X.Y.0"); writes patch the 16-byte
    value in place with a CRC16 (Modbus poly 0xA001, init 0xFFFF,
    LE on the wire) of bytes 0-13 appended at bytes 14-15.
  fff6 (notify) + fff8 (write, single byte) — on-device history
    (data-logger) download: write 2 = request temperature header,
    4 = humidity header; 1/3 = request temperature/humidity content;
    7/8 = request temperature/humidity CRC. Header notification is
    6 bytes: u32 LE sample count + CRC16 of the first 4 bytes.
    Each complete group of 10 samples is stored as two signed int16 LE
    endpoints (4 bytes) and linearly interpolated. Define
    compressed_len = ((count - count % 10) / 10) * 4. Compressed
    notifications are zero-padded to 20-byte boundaries. The raw
    remainder starts at ceil(compressed_len / 20) * 20, NOT at
    compressed_len, and contains count % 10 signed int16 LE values with
    no interpolation. Values are x100 device units; timestamps derive
    from the fff1 interval counted back from request time. The final
    CRC16-Modbus covers the meaningful compressed bytes followed
    immediately by the meaningful raw remainder, excluding every
    notification-padding byte. Header CRC covers only the first four
    count bytes.
  fff9 (write, single byte) — 0x01 = clear logged history,
    0x06 = graceful disconnect request.

OTA: the app updates firmware over BLE with PhyPlus SLB/SHB. SHB takes Intel HEX (.hex/.hex16), writes 01 02 with response to 5833ff02-… for those images (01 03 for resource images), then disconnects and rescans for PPlusOTA. SLB takes raw binary. OTA mode uses the normal address's last octet +1. SHB roles are service 5833ff01-…, command 5833ff02-…, notify 5833ff03-… and no-response data 5833ff04-…; SLB roles are service 0000feb3-…, command 0000fed5-…, no-response data 0000fed7-… and notify 0000fed8-…. Whether either OTA service UUID is advertised, and whether signatures are enforced, remain unknown. Firmware metadata comes from POST https://api-inkbird.com/api/bleDevice/firmware with a JSON body {bleDeviceName, bleVersion}; the response carries the download URL.
FAMILY CROSS-REFERENCE: Inkbird ships several incompatible protocols under similar names, and 0000fff0 is shared between them:
  - This spec: IBS-TH1/TH2/P01B sensors, names "sps"/"tps", 9-byte ads.
  - iBBQ-1/2/4/6 BBQ thermometers also advertise the fff0 service but
    with names containing "iBBQ"/"xBBQ" and 12/14/18/22-byte
    manufacturer data (probe temps at the tail) — see the sibling spec
    ibbq-meat-thermo (0xfff0 binary GATT protocol, app com.inkbird.ibbtgo).
  - IBT-2X/IBT-4XS/IBBQ-4BW use the 0000ff00 ASCII-hex command protocol
    — see the sibling spec inkbird-bbq-thermometer.
Discriminate by local name + manufacturer-data length + service UUID, never by service UUID alone.

credentials.notes: BLE advertisement broadcast, no auth. No Wi-Fi on this model family.

factory_reset.effect: No factory reset exists or is needed: the device holds no credentials, bindings or client state. Removing the battery for 10+ seconds is the only reset relevant to a BLE client — the device simply resumes broadcasting.

methods.description: Match local name "sps"/"tps" and the fff0 service UUID, take the 9-byte manufacturer data, decode temperature, humidity and battery. Byte 8 == 0x06 selects the app's connected-onboarding route (one fff2 read); other values stay advertisement-only.

steps.action: Insert the battery; the sensor starts advertising immediately.
Scan for name sps/tps with service UUID 0000fff0 and a 9-byte manufacturer-data AD structure.
Decode temperature (bytes 0-1, s16 LE, /100), humidity (bytes 2-3, u16 LE, /100), battery (byte 7), and onboarding route (byte 8).
steps.expect: Live readings with every advertisement; humidity above 100% marks a corrupt packet — drop it.

steps.action: If byte 8 is 0x06, connect and read fff2 once for live data; otherwise remain advertisement-only.

setup.notes: No provisioning, pairing, bonding or account. The device advertises as soon as a battery is fitted; readings are decoded passively. Confidence high: the decode is pinned by captured advertisements in the inkbird-ble test suite and runs in production in the Home Assistant core inkbird integration.

rejoin.notes: Broadcast-only with no bond: any number of clients can decode the advertisements, and switching controllers is just scanning from the new one.

variants.notes: Temperature + humidity + battery in the 9-byte advertisement.
Same 9-byte format. Humidity field reads 0 on units without a humidity sensor (the P01B pool thermometer); report humidity only when non-zero (inkbird-ble behaviour).

entities.name: Humidity
entities.notes: IBS-TH1 only; IBS-TH2/P01B reports 0 when no humidity sensor is fitted — suppress zero.

entities.name: Battery
entities.notes: Advertisement byte 7 only; not present in the GATT poll.

dfu_mode.notes: The OTA address increments the normal address's last octet modulo 256: (last + 1) & 0xFF, so 0xFF wraps to 0x00. SHB serves 5833ff01-… (command ff02, notify ff03, no-response data ff04); SLB serves 0000feb3-… (command fed5, no-response data fed7, notify fed8). Whether those UUIDs are advertised remains unknown. "PPlusOTA" is a generic PhyPlus name: tie it to this sensor only after starting an update and matching the expected address.

enter.notes: For SHB .hex/.hex16, write 01 02 with response to 5833ff02-…; 01 03 selects resources. Then disconnect and rescan for PPlusOTA. SLB uses raw binary and the fed5/fed7/fed8 roles below, but its application-mode entry bytes are not established.

image.format: SHB: Intel HEX (.hex/.hex16); SLB: raw binary.
image.notes: The app POSTs {bleDeviceName, bleVersion} as JSON to https://api-inkbird.com/api/bleDevice/firmware; the response carries the image's download URL. Local SHB images are Intel HEX; raw binary is the SLB input. Signature enforcement is UNKNOWN — the app's unused optional AES path is not evidence of unsigned images.

dfu.notes: App-derived and corroborated by SHB UUIDs in stock firmware; no update or address transition was run against hardware.

IBS_TH_Advertisement.description: 9-byte manufacturer-specific AD structure (type 0xFF). Byte 0 is the start of the AD content — the pseudo company-ID position that actually carries the temperature.

fields.description: Bytes 0-1, signed int16 LE, /100.0 °C. Surfaces to BLE stacks as the manufacturer-data company id.
fields.name: temperature

fields.description: Bytes 2-3, uint16 LE, /100.0 % RH. Drop the packet if decoded humidity exceeds 100% (corrupt).
fields.name: humidity

fields.description: Byte 4: channel-layout selector 0-3; decides which bytes carry internal vs external-probe values (see device.notes). Bytes 5-6: secondary channel value, signed int16 LE, /100.0 (external temp or humidity per selector).
fields.name: channel_selector

fields.description: 0x06 = connect and read fff2 once during onboarding; other values, including 0x08, = advertisement-only. Client behavior, not a hardware revision.
fields.name: onboarding_route

parse_rules: byte 4 = channel selector 0-3; bytes 5-6 = secondary channel value s16le / 100.0 (see device.notes for the per-selector mapping)
If byte 8 == 0x06 during onboarding, connect and read fff2 once; otherwise keep the advertisement-only route. Do not infer a hardware revision from this byte.
Do not match or filter on the company-ID position; it is data.

format.name: humidity
format.notes: Reads 0 on units without a humidity sensor (IBS-TH2/P01B); report only when non-zero.

characteristics.name: sensor_data
characteristics.notes: Current reading, same field layout as the advertisement head: temperature int16 LE /100 °C at bytes 0-1, humidity at bytes 2-3 (the official app reads humidity as signed int16). Byte 4 is a probe/channel indicator consumed by the app. No battery byte here — battery is only in the advertisement.

characteristics.name: config
characteristics.notes: 16-byte config block (from the Engbird app): bytes 1-2 internal temp calibration (s16 LE, x0.01 °C), bytes 3-4 external probe temp calibration, bytes 5-6 humidity calibration, bytes 7-10 logging interval (u32 LE seconds), bytes 11/13 ASCII firmware version digits. Writes patch the block in place; bytes 14-15 carry CRC16 (Modbus poly 0xA001, init 0xFFFF) of bytes 0-13.

characteristics.name: history_data
characteristics.notes: Streams the on-device log in response to fff8 commands. Header: u32le count + CRC16-Modbus of the four count bytes. Content: compressed_len = ((count - count % 10) / 10) * 4 bytes of signed-LE endpoints (two per ten samples), zero-padded to 20-byte notification boundaries. Raw remainder starts at ceil(compressed_len / 20) * 20 and holds count % 10 signed-LE values. Final CRC16-Modbus covers meaningful compressed bytes followed by meaningful raw remainder, excluding notification padding. Values are x100 device units.

characteristics.name: history_command
characteristics.notes: Single-byte history commands: 2 = temperature header, 1 = temperature content, 7 = temperature CRC; 4 = humidity header, 3 = humidity content, 8 = humidity CRC.

characteristics.name: control
characteristics.notes: Single-byte control: 0x01 = clear logged history, 0x06 = graceful disconnect.

services.name: Inkbird Sensor Service
services.notes: Shared with the iBBQ BBQ-thermometer family — do not treat the service UUID alone as identification. Connected access is optional; the advertisement carries every field.

enter_ota_hex.advanced_reason: Reboots into firmware-update mode and interrupts normal sensor service; have the exact matching image ready.
enter_ota_hex.description: Enter OTA for an Intel HEX .hex/.hex16 application image, then disconnect and rescan for PPlusOTA at address last-octet +1.

enter_ota_resources.advanced_reason: Reboots into firmware-update mode and interrupts normal sensor service; have the exact matching resource image ready.
enter_ota_resources.description: Enter OTA for a resource image, then disconnect and rescan for PPlusOTA at address last-octet +1.

characteristics.name: SHB OTA Data
characteristics.notes: Bulk firmware data; no-response writes in the app's update path.

services.name: PhyPlus SHB OTA Service
services.notes: SHB update path reported by the app's update implementation. Command writes use response; bulk data uses write-without-response. The stock firmware image also contains these SHB UUIDs. No update was executed.

characteristics.name: SLB OTA Command
characteristics.notes: Command writes use response; no application-mode entry bytes are asserted.

services.name: PhyPlus SLB OTA Service
services.notes: SLB raw-binary update path (reported); its application-mode entry trigger is not established.
